[F006] All green and evidence refreshed. Here's the summary.

The single high/correctness finding from codex-auditor F006-i1 — that the public `dontpanic doctor` paths still attempt an invocation-ledger write (cli.py:5751-5769 wrapping every CLI invocation in `start_recording(...).finalize(...)`, appending to `invocations.jsonl`), violating D050's "plain doctor and upgrade report perform ZERO writes (...ledger...)" invariant — is now fixed at the ledger seam itself. I added a `_ZERO_WRITE_COMMANDS = frozenset({"doctor"})` set plus `is_zero_write_command()`/`_first_command()` helpers in `invocation_ledger.py`, and made `start_recording` return the existing `_NullRecorder()` (no-op finalize) for the read-only `doctor` command before any bootstrapping, so the public wrapper records nothing for plain `doctor`, `--upgrade`, `--upgrade --json`, and `--check-upstream` while the `finally: recorder.finalize(...)` in `cli.main` stays untouched for every other command. I verified the live repro the auditor ran — `python -m dontpanic_orchestrate doctor --upgrade --json` and plain `doctor --skip-auth` against an isolated `DONTPANIC_HOME` produce no `invocations.jsonl`, while `ps` still writes one. I added two regression tests in `test_doctor_upgrade_render_f006.py` (`test_invocation_ledger_skips_doctor_command` asserting the no-op recorder and command classification, and `test_cli_main_doctor_writes_no_ledger_line` driving the actual `cli.main(["doctor", ...])` wrapper and asserting zero ledger
